title: Grundgesetz — human dignity & inviolable rights (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Article 1 anchors human dignity and binds state authority to respect and protect fundamental rights. Rights are legally binding on legislature, executive, and judiciary, with mechanisms including constitutional complaint in appropriate cases.

title: Personal freedom & rule-of-law guarantees (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Basic Law protects life, personal freedom, equality before the law, faith and conscience, expression, assembly, privacy of correspondence, and property, each with statutory limits where expressly contemplated.

title: Federal order — Länder & Bund (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Germany is a federal republic dividing competences between the Federation and the Länder. Exclusive, concurrent, and framework legislative powers determine who regulates topics like civil law, police law, and education.

title: Federal Constitutional Court role (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Federal Constitutional Court reviews statutes and official acts for compatibility with the Basic Law, including individual constitutional complaints. Its decisions shape the meaning of fundamental rights over time.
